S01: In the city of Tiryns, behind walls of enormous stone, lived an old resentment.
S02: Queen Stheneboea could not sleep from the insult.
S03: For her it was unforgivable — and the guest must pay.
S04: Stheneboea: "I want his blood! Remove Bellerophon!"
S06: Proetus: "I cannot. The gods forbid us to harm our guest."
S07: The law of guests was older and stronger than any wrath.
S08: Then, in him was born a cunning thought.
S09: He would send him where no one returns.
S10: Proetus: "You shall go against the Chimera. No one has ever survived."
S11: And in the courtyard, beneath the early sun, waited the young guest.
S12: The task reached him like a heavy, cold curse.
S13: Fear would not stop him — it would only sharpen him.
S14: With his faithful Pegasus, Bellerophon rose into the sky.
S15: They flew over wild lands, toward the place where no one goes.
S16: Bellerophon looked ahead — and knew he must not err.
S17: There, above a cracked mountain, rose smoke like a warning.
S18: Then, from the darkness came the being that could not be described in words.
S19: Lion's head, goat's body and serpent's tail — all in one.
S20: Its maw was a furnace, and its eyes — two embers.
S21: Bellerophon did not flinch — he measured, he did not fear.
S22: He needed no sword — but a cold-blooded mind.
S23: The monster flew at them, carrying fire like a spear.
S24: From its breast rose a wave of fire.
S25: And then — a blaze. Only so could the flames be quenched.
S26: With one swoop, they parted the sky and descended toward the earth.
S27: With the blade he dug out several heavy, grey lumps from the earth.
S28: From the heat, the lead melted into a liquid, gleaming metal.
S29: They rose again, carrying the liquid metal as a secret weapon.
S30: All was ready — only the true moment remained.
S31: The Chimera opened its mouth to swallow him with fire.
S32: It gaped like an open furnace in the sky.
S33: But Bellerophon was swifter than the fire itself.
S34: And in the last instant, he poured the lead precisely into the open mouth.
S35: The metal hardened in an instant — and the monster fell silent.
S36: The lead set and quenched the fire from within.
S37: And so, the monster from which all fled — fell.
S38: Above remained only the victor and his inseparable friend.
S39: Morning covered the mountain with a peaceful, rosy light.
S40: In full sun, Bellerophon landed before the walls of Tiryns.
S41: In his eyes mingled weariness and earned pride.
S42: Before the king, he stood alive — proof that even an impossible path exists.
S43: Proetus: "All is forgiven. You brought victory to our city."
S44: Never before had he looked so — with gratitude.
S45: Bellerophon bowed — not from submission, but from peace.
S46: The palace, once cold, now shone with reconciliation.
S47: And outside, his winged friend awaited him.
S48: And together, they flew toward many new adventures.
